findings.F1: The tested link is concentrated in its extreme corner. Days with volume over 2.5 times the prior 20-day mean that closed in the bottom fifth of their range were followed by a next-day excess return of +3.19 % (t 4.14, 102 cases), and those with volume 1.5–2.5 times by +1.05 % (t 3.41, 310 cases). Every other volume-by-close cell sits between −0.55 % and +0.42 %, with |t| below 1.6. With volume over 2 and close location above 0.8, all six coins are positive (+1.25 % to +3.37 %) and seven of eight years are positive.
findings.F2: On the tested product of close location and volume ratio, the top quintile's excess return over the next two days, on a non-overlapping 2-day grid, is +0.92 % (t 4.29, 1445 cases). The other four quintiles are all negative (−0.13 % to −0.35 %). On the 3-day grid the top quintile gives only +0.58 % (t 1.88), so the move is mostly over within two days.
findings.F3: On down days, the wider the range against the prior 20-day mean range, the higher the next-day excess return (slope t 6.06, 7144 down days). Up days show no such rise: the widest-range quintile gives −0.27 %, t −1.65.
findings.F4: In the widest-range quintile of down days, the next-day excess return is positive in all six coins (+0.54 % to +1.22 %, t 1.43 to 3.78) and in all eight years (+0.17 % to +1.70 %). Within that quintile, heavy-volume days give +1.16 % (t 5.41, 864 cases) and normal-volume days +0.35 % (t 1.61).
findings.F5: Measured in units of the coin's prior 20-day volatility, falls of 1 to 1.5 are followed by +0.62 % (t 3.52, 861 cases) and falls of 2 to 3 by +0.61 % (t 2.34). Small rises of 0 to 1 are followed by about −0.2 % (t −2.3 to −2.5).
findings.F6: In a joint regression of the next-day excess return, close location × volume ratio keeps t 6.30 and the size of the fall in volatility units keeps t 2.50. The range ratio is negative (t −2.87) when up and down days are pooled.
findings.F7: Among days falling more than 1.5 volatility units, heavy-volume days that closed in the bottom 30 % of their range gave +1.60 % next day (t 4.70, 331 cases). The other three groups were within ±0.7 % (|t| ≤ 1.34).
findings.F8: The book's daily returns track the coins closely (correlation 0.77, slope 0.39). Positions average 0.42 and are above 0.01 on 88 % of bars. The middle forecast quintile still holds 0.25 while its next-day excess return is −0.14 %, so ordinary days are held at a cost.
findings.F9: The next-day excess return after the Friday bar is +0.30 % (t 3.76, 2479 cases), positive in all six coins. It is negative in 2018, 2022 and 2023, and among seven weekdays it does not stand out enough to count.

ideas.idea: On a day that falls, the wider that day's high-low range is against the coin's average range over the prior 20 days, the more the coin rises over the next day.
ideas.consequence: A trader buys for one day after a down day whose range has blown out against its recent norm, and buys more the wider the range, rather than selling into the expansion.
ideas.name: wide-range down-day rebound

ideas.idea: On a day of heavy volume against the coin's prior 20-day average, the lower the close sits within the day's high-low range and the heavier the volume, the more the coin rises over the next two days.
ideas.consequence: A trader holds the absorption long for two days rather than one, so that each trade captures a move well above its cost.
ideas.name: absorption rebound over two days

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's one-day fall against its own 20-day volatility, and the lower that day's close sits within its range on heavy volume against its prior 20-day average, the more the coin rises over the next day.
ideas.consequence: A trader sizes the one-day rebound long by how many volatility units the coin fell and how close to its low it closed on heavy volume, and refuses the long after mild or high-closing falls.
ideas.name: volatility-scaled capitulation rebound
